full_judgment:
4. The defendant Nos. 1-3 and their father, the defendant No. 4, contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations and contending that the suit is not maintainable being barred by the principle of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence and by limitation. Their specific case is that the land covering an area of 0.97 acre of the disputed plot admittedly belonged to Khodeza Khatun and the SA record was correctly prepared in her name. Out of the said plot, 0.04 acres of land is situated in front of their residence, and the same was transferred to the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 by the said Khodeza Khatun, they purchased the same in the name of their sons the defendant Nos. 1-3 by the disputed kabala dated 7-6-1986 and got its possession, since then they have been enjoying and possessing the same. The affidavit, as allegedly sworn by Khodeza Khatun, is a fictitious document. She did never swear any such affidavit. The plaintiffs never got possession over that 0.04 acre of land purchased by them. After purchase by erecting tin shed thereon they have been running their business. Though they purchased 0.04 acres of land but they got the possession only in 0.03 acre. Their such purchased land has already been mutated in their names. The plaintiffs have/had no title and possession over that land. It is further contended that the market value of disputed land is not less than Taka 1,50,000 and the suit was not properly valued and stamped. The suit is not maintainable without a prayer for partition. The story of acquisition of land by the Government for construction of road is not correct. There was no such road and the story of acquisition and requisition alleged by the plaintiffs is false. In their additional written statement the said defendants also stated that the land measuring an area of 0.97 acre of the disputed plot and other undisputed land covering an area of 2.07 acre of RS Khatian No. 555 was recorded in the name of Nurun Nabi Sarker. The land of the disputed khatian and other lands originally belonged to Kanai Sheikh under the landlord Goyabari Liton Company Limited. Kanai Sheikh settled the land from disputed and undisputed holding to the said Nurun Nabi Sarker by issuing Dakhila in the last part of 1347 BS. The rent receiving interest of the said landlord Goyabari Liton Company Limited was transferred to one Mohamoyee Dashya and others. After enforcement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the said Nurun Nabi Sarker became a tenant under the Government and the said Nurun Nabi Sarker transferred the suit land and other lands to Khodeza Khatun from whom the defendants purchased the alleged 0.04 acre. 

 7. Mr Hasan Foez Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that both the Courts below failed to find that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. Mr Siddique further submits that admittedly. Khodeza Khatun was the owner of the suit land, as per the plaintiffs they purchased only 0.24 acre of land out of 0.97 acre of land of the disputed plot and some other persons also purchased land from the said plot sold by said Khodeza Khatun by different Kabalas and for construction of Assam Access Military Road some land was also acquired from the said plot, as per the plaintiffs except their predecessor none of the purchasers got possession of actual quantum of land as mentioned in the sale deeds. As such, without a prayer for partition the suit is not maintainable. He further submits that if the quantum of acquired land is treated as correct the said Khodeza Khatun had got no saleable interest after such acquisition and she was not in a position to sell any land allegedly purchased by the predecessor of plaintiffs. He further submits that in passing the impugned judgments the Courts below illegally based on the report of the Assistant Commissioner (land) but that report is not admissible as evidence under law, the impugned judgment based on such inadmissible evidence is not sustainable. In support of his such contention Mr Siddique cited the decision in the case of Enjaheruddin Mia vs Mohammad Hossain reported in 1998 BLD (AD) 77 = 50 DLR (AD) 84, Mahtab Ali vs Kartick Chandra Karmakar reported in 3 BLC 349, AIR 1928 Calcutta 62, AIR 1936 Oudh 192.
